judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Breathless exclamations, '--' dash and 'lad' all fit Nox, but the city-and-express-elevator framing and the tidy key-then-chest-then-secret-passage walkthrough read like a careful reconstruction of the mine quests; a close call.

items.label: B
items.critique: Too literary and too loaded with plot for Nox: a mystery seeded through a hooded man, 'Hmmm... Yes.', a robe given as reward and a handoff to another master. Westwood's rescues are blunter and shorter.

items.label: C
items.critique: Pure Westwood melodrama: 'Damn! Where have you been, lad!?', run-on exposition from the captive about mana and enchantments, and the clumsy 'At happier other times'. Nobody imitating would write that last phrase.

items.label: D
items.critique: Plain, short and comic. The 'What's that you say? Heaps and heaps of gold?' gag in the reward is the deadpan player-greed joke Nox makes, and 'However can I repay you' has its period quaintness.

items.label: E
items.critique: Terse to the point of thinness: 'Help us!', 'damsels', 'my boy' and the abrupt 'Now go find the other two groups' are Westwood's quick, slightly crude mass-rescue writing.

items.label: F
items.critique: 'What took you so long to get here!?', 'Nox's vital interests', a counted, mechanical journal entry ('Charm or kill all the monsters... Rescue the 6 trapped mine workers') and the Captain's message tacked on are all authentic campaign texture.

items.label: G
items.critique: A near beat-for-beat copy of D's structure and joke ('What's that you say? A great big sack of gold?'), swapped onto a novice and Urchins. The template shows, and 'Wanderer' as an address is not Nox's.

items.label: H
items.critique: Competent but generic: a guildmaster, a bell tower, gatemen and 'I insist'. The reminder repeats its own urgency in three short exclamations, and the dialogue lacks Westwood's odd specifics and run-on energy.

tells: Westwood's lines carry odd, slightly clumsy phrasing ('At happier other times', 'Nox's vital interests') and run-on exposition; the new texts are smoother and more evenly paced.
Westwood's journal entries are flat and mechanical, sometimes with counts ('Rescue the 6 trapped mine workers'); new journal entries read as composed summaries with possessive chains.
New texts seed side mysteries and handoffs (a hooded figure, a robe, 'tell Master X I sent you') that Westwood's single rescue quests rarely bother with.
When a Westwood joke is reused, the new text copies its structure line for line; one-to-one parallels between two texts point to the imitator.
Westwood addresses the player as 'lad', 'my boy' or 'young sir' and shouts with '!?'; invented forms of address such as 'Wanderer' or 'Kind sir' plus 'I insist' read as another writer.
